verses.english: Linked Discourses 35.74
8. Sick
Sick (1st)
At Sāvatthī.

verses.pali: Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami …pe… ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: Then a mendicant went up to the Buddha, and said to him,

verses.pali: “amukasmiṁ, bhante, vihāre aññataro bhikkhu navo appaññāto ābādhiko dukkhito bāḷhagilāno.
verses.english: “Sir, in such and such a monastery there’s a mendicant who is junior and not well-known. He’s sick, suffering, gravely ill.

verses.pali: Sādhu, bhante, bhagavā yena so bhikkhu tenupasaṅkamatu anukampaṁ upādāyā”ti.
verses.english: Please go to him out of sympathy.”

verses.pali: Atha kho bhagavā navavādañca sutvā gilānavādañca, “appaññāto bhikkhū”ti iti viditvā yena so bhikkhu tenupasaṅkami.
verses.english: When the Buddha heard that the mendicant was junior and ill, understanding that he was not well-known, he went to him.

verses.pali: Addasā kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ dūratova āgacchantaṁ.
verses.english: That mendicant saw the Buddha coming off in the distance
and stirred in his cot.

verses.pali: Atha kho bhagavā taṁ bhikkhuṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: The Buddha said to that monk,
“It’s all right, mendicant, don’t get up.
There are some seats spread out, I will sit there.”
He sat on the seat spread out

verses.pali: Nisajja kho bhagavā taṁ bhikkhuṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: and said to the mendicant,

verses.pali: “kacci te, bhikkhu, khamanīyaṁ, kacci yāpanīyaṁ, kacci dukkhā vedanā paṭikkamanti no abhikkamanti, paṭikkamosānaṁ paññāyati no abhikkamo”ti?
verses.english: “I hope you’re keeping well, mendicant; I hope you’re all right. I hope that your pain is fading, not growing, that its fading is evident, not its growing.”

verses.pali: “Na me, bhante, khamanīyaṁ, na yāpanīyaṁ, bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti no paṭikkamanti, abhikkamosānaṁ paññāyati no paṭikkamo”ti.
verses.english: “Sir, I’m not keeping well, I’m not getting by. The pain is terrible and growing, not fading; its growing is evident, not its fading.”

verses.pali: “Kacci te, bhikkhu, na kiñci kukkuccaṁ, na koci vippaṭisāro”ti?
verses.english: “I hope you don’t have any remorse or regret?”

verses.pali: “Taggha me, bhante, anappakaṁ kukkuccaṁ, anappako vippaṭisāro”ti.
verses.english: “Indeed, sir, I have no little remorse and regret.”

verses.pali: “Kacci pana taṁ, bhikkhu, attā sīlato upavadatī”ti?
verses.english: “I hope you have no reason to blame yourself when it comes to ethical conduct?”

verses.pali: “Na kho maṁ, bhante, attā sīlato upavadatī”ti.
verses.english: “No sir, I have no reason to blame myself when it comes to ethical conduct.”

verses.pali: “No ce kira te, bhikkhu, attā sīlato upavadati, atha kiñca te kukkuccaṁ ko ca vippaṭisāro”ti?
verses.english: “In that case, mendicant, why do you have remorse and regret?”

verses.pali: “Na khvāhaṁ, bhante, sīlavisuddhatthaṁ bhagavatā dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāmī”ti.
verses.english: “Because I understand that the Buddha has not taught the Dhamma merely for the sake of ethical purity.”

verses.pali: “No ce kira tvaṁ, bhikkhu, sīlavisuddhatthaṁ mayā dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāsi, atha kimatthaṁ carahi tvaṁ, bhikkhu, mayā dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāsī”ti?
verses.english: “If that is so, what then do you understand to be the purpose of teaching the Dhamma?”

verses.pali: “Rāgavirāgatthaṁ khvāhaṁ, bhante, bhagavatā dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāmī”ti.
verses.english: “I understand that the Buddha has taught the Dhamma for the purpose of the fading away of greed.”
“Good, good, mendicant!

verses.pali: Sādhu kho tvaṁ, bhikkhu, rāgavirāgatthaṁ mayā dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāsi.
verses.english: It’s good that you understand that I’ve taught the Dhamma for the purpose of the fading away of greed.

verses.pali: Rāgavirāgattho hi, bhikkhu, mayā dhammo desito.
verses.english: For that is indeed the purpose.
What do you think, mendicant?
Is the eye permanent or impermanent?”
“Impermanent, sir.” …
“Is the ear …
nose …
tongue …
body …
mind permanent or impermanent?”
“Impermanent, sir.”

verses.pali: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vā taṁ sukhaṁ vā”ti?
verses.english: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”
“Suffering, sir.”

verses.pali: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, kallaṁ nu taṁ samanupassituṁ:
verses.english: “But if it’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, is it fit to be regarded thus:
‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”
“No, sir.”

verses.pali: “Evaṁ passaṁ, bhikkhu, sutavā ariyasāvako cakkhusmimpi nibbindati, sotasmimpi nibbindati …pe… manasmimpi nibbindati.
verses.english: “Seeing this, a learned noble disciple grows disillusioned with the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

verses.pali: Nibbindaṁ virajjati; virāgā vimuccati; vimuttasmiṁ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṁ hoti.
verses.english: Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away they’re freed. When they’re freed, they know they’re freed.
They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended … there is nothing further for this place.’”
That is what the Buddha said.

verses.pali: Attamano so bhikkhu bhagavato bhāsitaṁ abhinandi.
verses.english: Satisfied, that mendicant approved what the Buddha said.

verses.pali: Imasmiñca pana veyyākaraṇasmiṁ bhaññamāne tassa bhikkhuno virajaṁ vītamalaṁ dhammacakkhuṁ udapādi:
verses.english: And while this discourse was being spoken, the stainless, immaculate vision of the Dhamma arose in that mendicant:
“Everything that is liable to arise is liable to cease.”
